title: Keyestudio KS0414 Turbidity Sensor V1.0 - Vendor Documentation

chunks.locator: Description, Specification, Output behaviour and Vendor notices - "the lower the output voltage is"

claims.claim: The KS0414 vendor specification gives a detection range of 0% to 3.5%, labelled as 0 to 4550 NTU.
The KS0414 description prints its error range as "±05%F*S".
The KS0414 specification lists its error range as "±0.5%F*S".
For analog operation, set the KS0414 slide switch to A and connect its signal terminal to an analog port to read a value for calculating output voltage and turbidity.
claims.quote:
When slide the switch to A end, connect the signal end to analog port, can read the analog
value to calculate the output voltage so as to get the turbidity degree of water.

claims.claim: For digital operation, set the KS0414 switch to D and connect its signal terminal to a digital port to detect turbidity through a HIGH or LOW output.
claims.quote:
If slide to D
end, connect signal end to digital port, can detect the water whether is turbidity by outputting
HIGH or LOW level.

claims.claim: The KS0414 sensitivity can be adjusted by turning its blue potentiometer.
claims.quote: You can turn the blue potentiometer on the sensor to adjust the sensitivity of sensor.

claims.claim: The vendor lists rivers and streams, wastewater and effluent, sediment transport research, and laboratory measurements as turbidity-sensor applications.
claims.quote:
Turbidity sensors can be used in measurement of water quality in rivers and streams, wastewater
and effluent measurements, sediment transport research and laboratory measurements.

claims.claim: The KS0414 specification lists DC 5 V operating voltage and about 11 mA operating current.
claims.quote:
- Operating Voltage: DC 5V
- Operating Current: about 11mA

claims.claim: The KS0414 specification lists operating temperatures of -30 to 80 °C and storage temperatures of -10 to 80 °C.
The KS0414 specification lists a weight of 18 g.
The KS0414 output voltage decreases as turbidity increases.
claims.quote:
The corresponding table of output voltage and concentration shows that the higher the turbidity
value is, the lower the output voltage is.

claims.claim: The vendor labels its conversion empirical and equates 1 mg/L with 0.13 NTU and 3.5% with 35000 mg/L or 4550 NTU.
The document states that the vendor percentage-to-NTU conversion is not a calibration against turbidity standards and that no output-voltage-to-NTU equation is published.
claims.quote:
It is not a calibration
against turbidity standards, and the vendor publishes no equation relating output voltage to NTU;

claims.claim: Only the transparent bottom part of the KS0414 probe may be placed in water because the probe top is not waterproof.
claims.quote: Note: the top of probe is not water-proof; can only place the transparent bottom part into water.

chunks.locator: Vendor notices and Properties this vendor documentation does not state - "The top of probe is not water-proof"

claims.claim: The vendor warns that reversed power polarity or overvoltage can burn out the KS0414 and specifies DC 5 V only.
claims.quote:
Avoid burning out the sensor due to
reversed connection. The voltage can only be DC5V; pay close attention to the voltage to prevent
overvoltage from burning the sensor.

claims.claim: The KS0414 documentation does not identify the light source type or wavelength and does not establish whether it uses visible or infrared light.
claims.quote:
The light source type or its wavelength. Nothing on the page identifies the sensor as a white-light
  (visible) or an infrared instrument.

claims.claim: The KS0414 documentation does not give a detection angle or establish whether the measurement is nephelometric at 90 degrees or uses transmission.
claims.quote:
The angle at which scattered light is detected, so the page does not establish whether the
  measurement is nephelometric (90-degree) or a transmission measurement.

claims.claim: The KS0414 documentation mentions neither ISO 7027 nor EPA Method 180.1, FNU, or formazin.
claims.quote:
Neither ISO 7027 nor EPA
  Method 180.1 is mentioned, and neither the unit FNU nor the term "formazin" appears.

gaps: Gives no light-source type, wavelength, or detector angle, so it cannot establish visible versus infrared or nephelometric versus transmission measurement.
Gives no ISO 7027 or EPA Method 180.1 compliance claim, FNU designation, or formazin reference.
Gives no calibration procedure, calibration standards, factory calibration claim, or output-voltage-to-NTU equation.
Gives no response or settling time, linearity, minimum detection limit, resolution, or temperature-compensation specification.
Gives no dimensions, connector pinout, or depth rating beyond the warning to immerse only the transparent probe bottom.
Gives no numeric digital switching threshold or procedure for setting the potentiometer to a known NTU value.
Does not define F*S or resolve the different error-range notation in the description and specification.
summary.notes: Chunk 0 preserves conflicting error strings: the description says ±05%F*S and the specification says ±0.5%F*S; neither is corrected here. The empirical formula is rendered as 10-6 (PPM), with ambiguous exponent formatting, and is preserved literally. The characteristic curve and corresponding table are discussed but are not present as plotted or tabulated data in these chunks. Chunk 1 begins mid-word in its 400-character overlap and joins the repeated waterproofing notice directly to the Special Notice without whitespace. Overlap-only claims are assigned to chunk 0. The weight claim has no metric tag.
